objectives: This course is designed to provide you with a solid background for financial theory. This course will provide the students an overview of theoretical background on different topics, so the students will be prepared for studying advanced theory and exploring empirical idea. It is your responsibility to be well prepared in class. While going over the fundamentals without utilizing advanced mathematics, I expect the student to focus on broader topic and intuition instead of just the technical specifics. In addition, I expect you to be able to efficiently communicating the research agenda and implications starting from someone else’s work.
content: Intro; Consumption and production; Firm value, Financing and investment; Financial systems and governance; Micro foundation; Risk; Mean-variance portfolio choice, CAPM, APT and factor model; Other topics in asset pricing; Derivative pricing; Imperfect capital markets
books:
Text: Financial Economics (1st ed.) by Fabozzi, Neave, Zhou, Wiley, 2012 (https://tsanghai.com.tw/book_detail.php?c=537&no=3125)
Journal articles (if necessary)

•	Theoretical Foundations of Corporate Finance (1st ed.), by de Matos, Princeton University Press, 2001
•	Asset Pricing (Rev. ed.), by Cochrane, Princeton University Press, 2005
•	Theory of Asset Pricing (1st ed.), by Pennachi, Pearson, 2007
